questions.question: K-Means compares point x=[1,1] with centroids [0,0] and [5,5]. Which centroid receives the point?
options: The centroid [0,0]
The centroid [5,5]
Both centroids, because K-Means never assigns points
Neither, because centroids must be integers
questions.explanation: The distances are about 1.41 and 5.66, so the first centroid is closer.

questions.question: What does a high silhouette score generally indicate?
options: Every cluster contains exactly the same number of points
A point is close to its own cluster and far from neighboring clusters
The algorithm found the largest possible K
All input features have zero variance
questions.explanation: Silhouette compares within-cluster cohesion with separation from the nearest other cluster; values near 1 are favorable.

questions.question: In DBSCAN, what makes a point a core point?
options: It is the closest point to a K-Means centroid
It has the largest value on the first feature
It has at least min_samples points within the chosen eps neighborhood
It belongs to a cluster with exactly two dimensions
questions.explanation: DBSCAN grows clusters from dense neighborhoods. Border points can join a core point's cluster, while isolated points are noise.

questions.question: An elbow plot shows inertia falling sharply through K=3 and only slightly afterward. What is K=3 usually taken to be?
options: The only mathematically valid number of clusters
A sign that DBSCAN must be used instead
The number of features in the input matrix
A reasonable tradeoff between compactness and model complexity
questions.explanation: The elbow marks where adding another centroid yields diminishing improvement; it is a heuristic, not a proof of the true cluster count.

questions.question: Your data contain two crescent-shaped groups and isolated points. Which first choice matches those properties?
options: DBSCAN, with eps and min_samples tuned to the data density
K-Means with a very large K
A single Gaussian with a diagonal covariance
A supervised classifier trained without labels
questions.explanation: DBSCAN can find non-spherical connected regions and label sparse points as noise, unlike the spherical-centroid assumption of K-Means.

questions.question: How does a Gaussian Mixture Model differ from a hard K-Means assignment?
options: It can only return one cluster for the entire dataset
It assigns each point probabilities of belonging to each Gaussian component
It labels every low-density point as a missing value
It never estimates component means
questions.explanation: GMM uses soft responsibilities, allowing a point to be partly associated with several components while fitting their parameters with EM.
